newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-WEEKEND PROGRAMME IN ITALIAN SERIE A.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND PROGRAMME IN ITALIAN SERIE A.

text.p: Serie A games on Saturday and Sunday, kickoff times GMT:

Both sides have impending European games on their minds, Fiorentina against Spanish side Barcelona in the Cup Winners' Cup and Inter against French side Monaco in the UEFA Cup. Despite that consideration, this could be a tough encounter of the explosive kind between two full strength sides. Fiorentina's Argentine ace Gabriel Batistuta and Portuguese midfielder Rui Costa warmed up this week by taking high speed driving lessons with Ferrari Formula One driver, German Michael Schumacher. Inter rely on their attacking trio of Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff behind Chilean Ivan Zamorano and Maurizio Ganz.

Bologna are unlikely to show much mercy to second from bottom Reggiana in this Emilia Romagna derby. Bologna field their customary three-man attack of Carlo Nervo, Swede Kennet Andersson and Russian Igor Kolivanov, while Reggiana rely on another Russian, striker Igor Simutenkov.

There are some Roma fans who hope that Cagliari, led by former Roma coach Carlo Mazzone, will defeat Roma and thus precipitate a crisis which would see the club's Argentine coach Carlos Bianchi sacked. The disloyal fans may have their way since Cagliari are desperate for points while Roma will be without Argentine ace Abel Balbo and Francesco Totti, both suspended, while reserve striker Marco Delvecchio is doubtful through injury. Cagliari rely on Uruguayan Fabian O'Neill in midfield and experienced Sandro Tovalieri in attack.

Since Dino Zoff took over from Czech Zedenk Zeman at Lazio in late January, the Roman club have lost only once in seven games, picking up 14 points. With Giuseppe Signori back alongside Igor Protti in attack and with Australian Paul Okon returning from injury to replace Alessandro Nesta in defence, Lazio should continue their good run. Relegation battlers Piacenza have injury worries about defender Paolo Tramezzani and striker Pasquale Luiso.

UEFA Cup and/or Champions League participation is at stake in this battle with both sides relying on their attacking big guns, Enrico Chiesa and Argentine Hernan Crespo for Parma, Roberto Mancini and Vincenzo Montella for Sampdoria. Missing will be Sampdoria's injured Yugoslav defender Sinisa Mihajlovic.
Napoli might not thank you for saying so but this is a relegation battle. Perugia unveil new signing, Serb defender Bratislav Mijalkovic, while Napoli welcome the return of Brazilian Andre Cruz.

Beaten by AC Milan and Lazio in their last two games, Atalanta face another tough encounter against a Udinese side sitting too close to the relegation zone for comfort. Paolo Poggi and German Oliver Bierhoff lead the Udinese attack. Gigi Lentini and Filippo Inzaghi, top serie A goalscorer on 18, lead the Atalanta attack.

Having lost five of their last seven games, one time league leaders Vicenza could do with a boost and could well get one against Verona, another side seemingly destined for division two. Roberto Murgita and Uruguyan Marcelo Otero lead the Vicenza attack, while Verona field a cautious 4-5-1 with only Antonio De Vitis in attack.

It is strange to see Milan coming into this great classic of the Italian season 13 points behind arch rivals and league leaders Juventus. Even stranger to hear their charismatic captain Franco Baresi, playing in his 40th league and cup game against Juventus, suggesting that the best Milan can do this season will be to finish in the top six. With Dutchman Edgar Davids and Demetrio Albertini both injured, defender Alessandro Costacurta suspended and Liberian George Weah on international duty, Milan's prospects do not look good. Marco Simone and Frenchman Christophe Dugarry lead the Milan attack against a Juventus side led by Croat Alen Boksic and new national hero Christian Vieri, twice capped for Italy in the last week. For Juventus, Alessandro Del Piero and Moreno Torricelli are still out through injury while Uruguyan defender Paolo Montero and French midfielder Didier Deschamps are both suspended.
